# Tyrell allocation model and controlled callback contract

This package contains only the independently authored caller-supplied range/geometry model and controlled callback helpers. It contains two header-only helpers and two source fixtures, with their accepted private source bytes preserved exactly. There is no Tyrell inspector, original loader, factory, raw getter/setter, host ABI, audio processor, captured preset, decompiler output or commercial binary dependency.

Range addresses, lengths, owner relationships and proof booleans are supplied by the caller. A model `Ready` means its stated arithmetic/geometry prerequisites passed, not that an allocation is physically live, a logical object is initialized, a process is quiescent, an owner/table prefix is established or that a real pointer may be accessed. Caller spans, callbacks and scratch/destination storage must already be readable/live/disjoint as documented in the unchanged headers. Hostile pointer or callback validation is not offered. A failed primitive may partially change scratch/destination; the temporary pointer remains null on failure. Callback status values in the fixture are controlled0/4/5, not observed OS results.

The legacy fixture field `shared_production_callback_helper=true` denotes the shared source implementation; it is not a live production/readiness certificate. The separate private inspector's actual_quiescence_established, owner_logical_prefix_established and other_table_logical_spans_established gates remain false. That inspector and its machinery are not shipped or run here. No physical/logical spans, live bounds, native class/factory, state/audio/GUI/realtime or full-plugin equivalence is certified.

The standalone macOS recipe needs Python3, macOS clang++/codesign/lipo and support for executing own Intel products (Rosetta on Apple silicon). It uses only these eight package files and standard system toolchain selection; no private project, installed plugin, fixed SDK path or original binary is read. It compiles ranges/provider in normal and fatal ASan/UBSan/floatcast modes, exactly four own x86_64 products and twenty-four commands. Each product is ad-hoc signed, strictly verified and checked Intel before use. Complete stdout JSON is compared type-aware to twenty geometry rejections or twenty-five controlled callback cases; diagnostic output fails. These source tests do not establish natural allocator or original behavior.

For an authorized own-source validation run, a caller supplies verify.py with --expected-driver-sha256/bytes and --expected-manifest-sha256/bytes from the externally frozen package, a fresh --work with existing parent, and VL_TYRELL_ALLOCATION_CONTRACT_SOURCE_SLOT_GRANTED=1. Optimized Python and non-macOS hosts refuse before operations. No private recipe or archival evidence is needed to run it. The private eighteen mock recipe scenarios are historical review references only and are not shipped, replayed or inferred as coverage of this new recipe.

All eight source/control identities are declared before file reads and audited before compilation, before each product use, and at every final publication stage. Work creation is protected; output destinations precede writes/commands, captured logs/products retain their bytes, and final audits reconcile sealed identities. Primary, cleanup, recording and publication failures stay separate; result bytes alone are provisional and cannot override a failed caller. The source recipe uses only own Popen leaders/session groups and refreshes ownership before signalling. It does not independently prove arbitrary descendant closure or system toolchain/module completeness. File hashing is not a filesystem I/O wallclock certificate. Execution status and acceptance belong to separately pinned validation records; the protocol alone is not execution evidence.
